Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase of 74 runs by England. Dom Sibley and Zak Crawley walk out to the middle. The Sri Lankan team is also out there and no surprises as Lasith Embuldeniya will start with the ball.

Interesting to see how England players approach this target with the pitch showing its tricks. Sri Lanka would hope to get some early wickets and put pressure on the English middle order. All this coming up in a short while.

England bowlers had to work hard this time for their wickets as they were on the field for around 137 overs . Broad bowled very tight lines but was unlucky to not get any wickets. Curran bowled well and was rewarded with 2 wickets. Wood too tried all his short stuff but failed to take any wickets. The spinners Bess and Leach were the chief tormentors and finished with 3 and 5 wickets respectively. Now they would hope that the batsmen finish the job for the team.

The batting from Sri Lanka was pretty good as compared to their first innings. The openers laid the foundation with a solid 101-run stand. Perera scored a brilliant half ton but couldn't convert it into a big score. His partner, Thirimanne however went on to score his 2nd test ton and played beautifully for his 111. Angelo Mathews stood like a rock until the end scoring 71 runs. The middle order including the likes of Chandimal and Dickwella supported Angelo well and made sure that England have to bat again. The lower order batters also did their best to hang around with Mathews and give their bowlers something to defend.
So Sri Lanka have managed to score 359 runs and have given England a target of 74 when they come out to bat in the second innings.

Sri Lanka lead by 16 runs and would hope to bat out the day with Mathews and the remaining tail. England would look to clean up the tail and chase down the target today itself. An interesting last session coming up in around 20 minutes.

England bowlers had to toil hard in the middle. After getting rid of Chandimal early, they failed to get past the duo of Mathews and Dickwella for a long period. But just at the brink of tea, Bess got rid of Dickwella while Leach cleaned Shanaka up. Now that they have to bat again, they would look to get the remaining 3 wickets as quickly as possible.

Sri Lanka started off the session trailing by just 44 runs. Chandimal got out in the second over for a score of 20. But after that, the duo of Mathews and Dickwella did frustrate England with a 48-run stand. In the process, they managed to wipe out the deficit. But just when they would have looked to capitalize, Dickwella threw his wicket away and was followed by Shanaka soon. Mathews has been unbeaten on 51 but would want support from the other end if Sri Lanka have to put up a good score..

Sri Lanka almost won this session but gave away the advantage to England in the last half an hour losing 2 quick wickets. After losing Chandimal earlier after Lunch, the duo of Mathews and Dickwella managed to wipe out the deficit but Dickwella fell and was followed by Shanaka in the next over giving England a sniff to victory.

Sri Lanka's first target would be to get rid of the 44-run trail quickly without losing either of Chandimal or Mathews and then go towards setting a target for the opposition. Right then! Do join us for the second session in around 40 minutes to find out what happens.

England got the early wicket of Embuldeniya in the second over. The spinners created some chances with the ball bouncing and turning, but were unlucky to not get support from the fielders. The new ball finally helped them as Curran got the big wicket of Thirimanne. They leaked runs in this session and would like to build pressure on the batters in the upcoming period as they would not want to bat again with the huge target at their disposal.

Sri Lanka started off the day trailing by 130 runs. Night watchman Embuldeniya didn't do much and was out in the second over of the morning. The duo of Thirimanne and Mathews, then put on a good 52-run stand for the 3rd wicket. In the process, Thirimanne completed his 2nd Test ton. Just when the two were looking good, Thirimanne edged one off Curran with the second new ball and was dismissed on 111. The duo of Chandimal and Mathews have done well to play steady cricket and have kept the scoreboard ticking. They would hope to wipe out the 44 run deficit first post Lunch and then think for a target.

A session wherein 86 runs were scored and two wickets were taken should have been a shared session but in the context of the game it truly belongs to Sri Lanka. Thirimanne completed his 2nd Test ton while England have managed to eke out 2 wickets in this session including one of Thirimanne. But Sri Lanka would be more happy as they have reduced the deficit under 50.

Lahiru Thirimanne is down for a chat. Thirimanne says that they needed to fight back yesterday and their plan is to set a target of around 150. Says they discussed a few things in the dressing room, regarding playing each ball on the merit and taking calculative risks. He says he played on the merit of the ball and played well. Adds that pressure is part of the game. Reckons that the pitch is turning and the ball is misbehaving but they need to take some calculative risk to put a target of around 150.

Russell Arnold is down for the pitch report. He says that the pitch looks ugly for a batter. There are hardly any good areas amongst the rough patches on the pitch. Also adds that runs are easy to score at the square of the wicket. But the bowlers need to bowl above the batsmen's eyeline and make the batsmen play straight. Lot more work to be done by the Sri Lankan batters.

Welcome to Day 4 of the first Test between England and Sri Lanka. The moving day of the match yesterday saw Sri Lanka fight for another day. After restricting England to a score of 421 and conceding a lead of 286, Sri Lanka made a good start with both openers scoring half tons. The Lankans are still 130 runs behind, will they make England bat again or will the Englishmen bundle out the the hosts? Stay tuned with the morning session commencing soon.
... DAY 4, SESSION 1 ...

So Sri Lanka still trail by 130 runs and have 8 wickets in their kitty. Will they be able to clear the deficit or will England be able to wrap up the innings quickly? All questions will be answered on Day 4 tomorrow. Do join us at 0945 local (0415 GMT). Till then, take care and goodbye!

Joe Root is down for an interview. He starts by saying that he is happy with his knock. Adds that it was a good partnership with Jos Buttler. Mentions that it was a calm and composed knock from him. Praises Kane Williamson for his purple patch. Credits Paul Collingwood and Jacques Kallis for his improved batting. Root also says that they will look to take the remaining wickets quickly. Further says that there is enough turn and bounce on the track.

England bowlers bowled good line and lengths with Broad being at his miserly best. Curran was lucky to get the wicket of Perera. Wood too tried hard with his short ball stuff, but didn't get any wicket. The spinners Leach and Bess bowled well in patches, with the former getting rid of Mendis with a beautiful ball. They would look to exploit the conditions on offer in a better way tomorrow and would like to run through the Sri Lankan batting order.

After conceding a lead of 286 runs, Sri Lankan openers came out to bat with a positive mindset. Both Kusal Perera and Lahiru Thirimanne negated the early threat of Broad and then went on to play the spinners with ease. Soon after completing his 7th half ton, Perera threw his wicket away to a very poor ball. Kusal Mendis, coming off from 4 consecutive ducks stitched a nice 54-run stand with Thirimanne for the 2nd wicket, but was out to Leach at the fag end of the day. Thirimanne, meanwhile is still batting on 76 and would like to continue the same tomorrow.

Earlier in the morning, England started off the day with the duo of Jos Buttler and Joe Root scoring at a brisk rate. Root completed his 4th double ton and batted brilliantly for his 228. The tailenders didn't do much damage as Sri Lankan bowlers did make a comeback after a change of ball and restricted England for a total of 421. Dilruwan Perera was the pick of the bowlers for them as he took 4 wickets and got good support from Embuldeniya who got 3 and Asitha Fernando who got 2.

Well it is Stumps on Day 3! A good day of cricket comes to an end. Sri Lanka are still trailing by 130 runs but have done well throughout the day overall to still stay in the game. The last session saw 66 runs being scored by Sri Lanka with the loss of 2 wickets.

Sri Lanka would hope that the openers carry on with their good work after Tea until the close of play. England, meanwhile would look to get an opening and then capitalize on it. Final session of Day 3 coming up in a few minutes. Stay tuned.

England bowlers have bowled well but don't have any wickets to show for their work. Broad and Curran started with the new ball and did get some swing early on. But however were unable to get past the Sri Lankan openers. Mark Wood tested both the batters with some fiery short stuff, but couldn't eke out a wicket. England spinners Bess and Leach have tried to exploit the conditions but have hardly got any success. Skipper Root too rolled his arm over but was dealt away nicely by the batsmen.

Trailing by 286 runs, both the Sri Lankan openers have looked solid. Kusal Perera completed his 7th half century in Tests and has looked solid both against the seamers and the spinners, he did get hit on his hand a few minutes before Tea, but despite that has looked like a man on a mission. His partner Thirimanne too has played some lovely shots and has looked assured at the crease. The duo have managed to put an unbeaten 90-run stand and would like to continue the same after this break.
First session which we can say Sri Lanka has won convincingly in this match. They have scored 90 runs in this session and more importantly haven't lost a single wicket yet.
